Instead of mixing economic reasoning with programming details, a model can be written in a
designed specifically for economics and finance. Separating specification from implementation has several advantages:
– The specification remains close to the underlying economic logic, expressed in a concise and readable form. The modeler concentrates on
– The DSL uses syntax familiar to economists (equations, lags, variables), avoiding the clutter of general-purpose programming constructs.
– Models can be extended or updated without rewriting solution code. Changing an equation is as simple as editing one line in the specification.
– Once specified, the same model can be executed with different numerical engines or platforms without altering its economic content.
– The separation makes models easier to review, validate, and communicate, since the specification reads like economic theory rather than computer code.
